software-development: Ship code a senior would approve — test-first, your stack's patterns, nothing over-built.
data-analysis: Analyze data and grade AI output without fooling yourself.
rag-evaluation: Prove your RAG works — retrieval and answer, scored apart.
product-management: From fuzzy idea to shipped, measured feature — the whole PM toolkit.
application-security: Break it like an attacker, then write code that resists — audit to fix.
frontend-design: Interfaces people enjoy — polished, accessible, and alive.
web-research: A synthesized answer with sources — not 40 open tabs.
release-review: The last gate before ship — catch what a tired reviewer misses.
bug-fixing: Root cause, not symptom — fixed fast.
code-simplification: Delete the over-engineering — the best code is the code you didn't write.
content-writing: Docs and copy that sound human — not AI.
production-engineering: Design, ship, and run production systems — past 'works on my laptop'.
test-engineering: Tests that actually catch regressions — unit, end-to-end, and back.
sample-rag-evals: Sample custom kit. A small, focused kit for checking a RAG agent's answers. Edit it, delete it, or copy it as a starting point for your own.
sample-content-writing: Sample custom kit. A small kit for writing and cleaning up docs. Edit it, delete it, or copy it as a starting point for your own.
wiki: Document and onboard a codebase: understand a repo, generate a wiki and guided code tours, capture architecture and design decisions, and keep the docs useful.
product-frameworks: The three PM thinking frameworks most tools skip - Jobs to Be Done (why users come), Hook Model (why they stay), CRO (why they convert) - plus discovery and retention-measurement to apply them.
pm-methodology: A repeatable product methodology (product-on-purpose): one anchor skill per phase - Foundation, Discover, Define (JTBD), Develop, Deliver (PRD), Measure (experiments), Iterate (retro). Walk a product idea end to end.
